title: Reach law (c) passes a shank or holder collision on a tilted move: the skip disc follows the band, not the cutter

labels.name: P0
labels.description: Safety or crash: wrong output, gouge, data loss

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens: on a tilted move, `crates/sim/src/verify/reach.rs` (law (c), about lines 121-155) moves each band's test disc to the band's mid-axis position and then skips every sample within the cutter radius of that moved centre (`dd <= (r + gouge_tol)^2 -> continue`). On a tilted tool that disc is not material the cutter cleared - it lies under the band itself - so steel standing in the part there is never judged.

Evidence (high-tier review of PR #843, head f74f878d, https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/843#pullrequestreview-5864853674): wall at x 40, tip at (31, 50, -9), axis tilted 30 degrees toward the wall. A tool with no body and a slim holder (r6 x 20) is not convicted on that move on main's code path today; (c3) does not fire (no axis change on the move) and the solid law does not run (no model in a Boundary op). The same gap at the backstop's inner radius (reach.rs about line 175) and in the (c3) sweep discs.

Expected: the skip excludes only the cutter's own column (the volume the flutes really cleared along the tilted axis); a holder or shank inside the part on a tilted move is flagged and blocks the post.

Relation to #835 / PR #843: the band-stack change makes this reachable for stepped bodies too (the old wide cylinder's annulus hid it there), so the review blocked #843 on it. The fix is expected on #843's branch (`issue/835-...`), pinned for both a tilted body and a tilted plain holder, through (c) and (c3).

Done means: a test with the geometry above convicts the move for a plain slim holder and for a stepped body; the backstop and the (c3) sweep use the same corrected exclusion.
